newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks slump on disappointing Q1 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks slump on disappointing Q1 earnings.

text.p: Mexican stocks maintained their earlier slump to close lower on Monday on slow volume amid market disenchantment with first quarter earnings reports, traders and analysts said.

"It's all down to company earnings. There's been all this talk of an economic recovery, but in reports posted so far, we just don't see it yet," a desk trader said. "Mexican ADRs were hammered, but the Dow was fine."
The leading IPC share index ended down 26.43 points, or 0.70 percent, at 3,756.19. The Dow Jones meanwhile ended up 44.15 points at 6,783.02.
"The bourse moved erratically in the wake of first quarter 1997 earnings reports and has yet to define a positive or negative trend," a research report by the Valmex brokerage said.
"Earnings have shown little growth in sales, many firms still have financial problems and that's the big ones. Don't even look at the smaller ones," the desk trader added.
Dealers said ADRs listed by Telmex, down 7/8 to 40-5/8 weighed most on the slide in Mexican share prices. The telecomms firm's L shares ended down 14 centavos at 16.30 pesos.
Telmex was the most traded stock of the day, not counting cross trades, dealers said.
Dealers also drew attention to a poor performance by ADRs listed by beverage firm Coca-Cola Femsa, which dropped 2-3/4 to 33-1/2 while its peso shares fell 2.90 pesos to 26.90 pesos.
"Coca-Cola Femsa's bottom line earnings were apparently good, but only due to non-cash items," one trader said.
Televisa continued its recent slide on Wall Street, off 1-1/4 to 22-3/4, while the media group's CPO shares fell 1.90 pesos to 92.30 pesos in Mexico.

Some traders attributed Televisa's fall to a persistent adverse reaction to earnings posted last week, while others said the market was uneasy over a battle for boardroom control after the recent death of its long-serving chairman and president, Emilio Azcarraga Milmo.
"Televisa has many internal problems and that makes the market nervous," a trader said.
Shares listed by Bancomer, one of Mexico's biggest financial groups, slid two centavos to 2.75 pesos on profit-taking after gains last week coupled with fears of forthcoming interest rate rises.
Cross trades accounted for more than one-half the final trading volume figure of 90.3 million pesos and floor traders said dealing was quiet.
"Very slow, dealers are apprehensive over companies that still have to post earnings on Tuesday and Wednesday," a floor trader said.
Wednesday, April 30, sees the deadline for first quarter earnings reports in Mexico.
Traders said forecasts of slight falls in domestic interest rates did little to encourage stock buying.
"With the peso as weak as it is, cutting rates would be like scoring an own goal," one trader said.

A Reuters survey of money market traders showed they forecast the central bank would trim rates on bellwether 29-day Cetes by an average of 23 basis points to 20 percent at its weekly auction of government securities.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts had closed earlier a hefty 8.4 centavos weaker at 7.9700/7.9800 per dollar.
Auction results are due at 1830 local time/2330 GMT.
On the broad market, 107 stocks were traded, of which sliders outnumbered gainers by 59 to 25.
(( --Martin Roberts, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-7907))
